title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of type 2 diabetes and assessment of kidney function.

HPI
The patient presents for routine follow-up concerning his type 2 diabetes. He reports generally feeling well and adhering to his prescribed oral hypoglycemic regimen, taking metformin daily. He acknowledges his known chronic kidney disease stage 4. During today’s visit, the provider confirmed that the patient's current status of CKD stage 4 is unrelated to diabetes. He reports no recent changes in symptoms or medications.

Medication List
Metformin

Exam
Vitals are stable. Physical exam is unremarkable. No acute findings noted on cardiovascular or neurological examination.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Managed on metformin.
2. Chronic kidney disease stage 4: Status is known to be unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
Continue metformin as prescribed for type 2 diabetes. Follow up in three months for repeat laboratory studies. Patient educated on continued monitoring of kidney function.
explanations: The provider states the CKD is not due to diabetes, so the presumed link does not apply: code diabetes without complications and CKD separately.
Code also the CKD stage (N18.4) as instructed at the diabetes CKD code or separately when unrelated.
Long-term oral hypoglycemic use: add Z79.84.

distractors.why: The 'with' presumption is overridden when the provider documents another cause or no link.
The stage of CKD must be reported with N18.-.
Z79.84 captures long-term oral hypoglycemic use.
